reason: The sole paragraph of Executive Order 8341 says that Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940 "is hereby revoked." It is a present-tense, self-executing revocation with no deferred effective date, condition or continuing duty, so the command was performed and ended when the order was signed on February 8, 1940, the date printed in the held text. The filing date (February 9, 1940) and the issue date (February 10, 1940) are alternative readings, and none moves the end outside February 1940. The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 remains as a surviving effect of the completed act. No held instrument revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341.

Paragraph 1 closes the departments and agencies in the District of Columbia "all day on Tuesday, December 24,1940" and excuses employees from duty "on that day." The command therefore covers one calendar day and ended with that day by its own terms. The end is recorded as December 24, 1940, inclusive; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends it, and the exceptions in the paragraph do not extend its period.

Paragraph 2 directs that the order be published in the Federal Register. It is a one-time direction that was performed when the order appeared in the Federal Register issue dated Wednesday, December 18, 1940, as the masthead of the held page shows; the filing line in the held text gives the earlier date December 17, 1940, which is an alternative reading. After publication the paragraph has no further subject. No held instrument revokes, extends or amends it.

The clause revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska) and says that the order "shall become effective at the close of business January 15, 1941." The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment, so the command was performed and ended at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving effect of the completed act. No held instrument revokes, amends or restores the designation by executive order.
